claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown location is the Pacific Ocean roughly 50-80 miles offshore from San Diego, California.
The crew will complete a 10-day mission.
The reentry features a 3,000-degree fireball descent.
Artemis II marks the first crewed return from the Moon since 1972.
The crew and capsule will be recovered by US Navy ships.
According to CBS 8, the reentry fireball will appear in the northwestern sky.
The mission has a four-person crew.
The crew is returning from a 10-day loop around the Moon.
The mission tests deep-space systems in preparation for future lunar surface missions.
The capsule will separate from its service module before entering the atmosphere.
